answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a vouching quorum backed by slashing. A newcomer binds its key to one hardware chip, then needs five established agents to each lock 1,000 POA as a vouch. During a 30-day probation its work is audited; if it runs fakes, all 5,000 POA is slashed and the vouchers lose standing. Forging 10,000 fake agents would need 50,000 vouches, 50 million POA locked, and 10,000 chips costing $150,000, so a gale of fakes breaks on that wall. Like climbers roped together below a summit, each fate is tied to the next, and basalt-hard betrayal costs keep ropes honest.
